### | The Tenth Group

And another group have occupied their hours with the science of hadith — I mean its audition (samāʿ), the collection of its many narrations, and the pursuit of rare and elevated chains of transmission (asānīd). The aspiration of one of them is to journey through the lands and narrate from the shaykhs, so that he may say: "I narrate from so-and-so, and I saw so-and-so, and I met so-and-so, and I possess chains of transmission that no one else has." Their delusion (ghurūr) stems from several aspects: among them, they are like carriers of books (ḥamalat al-asfār), for they do not direct their care toward understanding the Sunnah and contemplating its meanings. Rather, they are confined to mere transmission (naql), and they suppose that this suffices them. How far from the truth! Nay, the very purpose of hadith is understanding and contemplating its meanings. The proper order in hadith is: first audition (samāʿ), then comprehension (tafahhum), then memorization (ḥifẓ), then action (ʿamal), then dissemination (nashr).

These people have confined themselves to audition without action — and moreover, they have not even mastered it. For even if there were no benefit in confining oneself to it, in this age they have children recite hadith while they are heedless and negligent; and the shaykh from whom one reads may himself be so heedless that were the text corrupted or altered, he would not know. Perhaps he even sleeps while hadith is narrated from him, and he is unaware. All of this is delusion. The fundamental principle in listening to hadith is that one hears it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or from the Companions, or from the Followers (tābiʿūn) — may Allah be pleased with them all. And one's hearing it from the Companions is like hearing it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he listens attentively and memorizes, and narrates it exactly as he memorized it, so that he does not doubt a single letter of it. If he doubts any of it, it is not permissible for him to narrate it. And the memorization of hadith occurs by two methods: the first is by the heart, with continuity through repetition and remembrance (dhikr). The second is that one writes as he hears, corrects what is written, and preserves it so that no hand of an alterer can reach it. And the preservation of the book requires that it be kept guarded in his library, so that no other hand can extend over it at all. Nor is it permissible to record the audition of a child, a heedless person, or a sleeper — for if that were permissible, one might record the audition of an infant in the cradle. And audition has many conditions.

The very purpose of hadith is to act upon it and to know it. It has many levels of meaning (mafhūmāt), just as the Qur'an does. It is narrated from one of the shaykhs that he attended a session of audition, and the first hadith he heard was the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: {«من حسن إسلام المرء تركه ما لا يعنيه»} ("From the perfection of a man's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him"). He stood up and said: "This suffices me until I have fully acted upon it, then I will hear others." Such is the audition of the intelligent. And this was Abū al-Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Khayr al-Munhī, who attended the session of Ibn Aḥmad al-Sarkhasī.

### | The Eleventh Group

And another group have occupied themselves with the science of grammar (naḥw), poetry, lexicography (lughah), and other such disciplines. They were deluded by it and claimed that it has secured their forgiveness, and that they are among the scholars of the Ummah — since the very foundation of religion and the Sunnah rests upon the science of language and grammar. So they squandered their lives upon the subtleties of grammar and lexicography. And that is delusion. For were they rational, they would know that the Arabic language is like the Turkish language; and the one who wastes his life upon the Arabic language is like the one who wastes his life upon Turkish or Indian. The only distinction of Arabic over them is the advent of the Sacred Law (sharʿ). Thus, what suffices of language is knowledge of the two "Gharībayn" (rare expressions) in the hadith and the Book, and of grammar, what pertains to the hadith and the Book. As for delving into endless degrees of depth, that is superfluous excess (fuḍūl) that is dispensable. Its practitioner is deluded.

### | The Second Class

### | Of the Deluded: The Masters of Devotions and Works

The deluded among them are many groups. Among them are those whose delusion lies in jihad (holy struggle), and among them are those whose delusion lies in asceticism (zuhd).

### | The First Group

Among them is a group who neglected the obligatory duties (farāʾiḍ) and occupied themselves with supererogatory acts (nawāfil). Perhaps they went to such extremes that they fell into extravagance and transgression — like the one whom obsessive doubt (waswās) overcomes in ablution (wuḍūʾ), so he overdoes it, and is not satisfied with water that the legal ruling (fatwā) declares pure, and he deems remote possibilities of impurity to be near. Yet when the matter turns to eating lawful food, he deems near possibilities to be remote, and perhaps he eats what is purely unlawful. Had he redirected this excess of caution from water to food, it would have been more fitting. And he would have resembled the conduct of the Companions — may Allah be pleased with them — for ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — performed ablution with water from a Christian woman's jar, despite the apparent possibility of impurity. And despite this, he would abandon many lawful doors out of fear of falling into the unlawful.

### | The Second Group

And another group are overcome by obsessive doubt in the intention (niyyah) of the prayer, so that Satan does not leave them to hold a sound intention. Rather, he whispers to them until they miss the congregation and the prayer exits its time. And if they complete the opening takbīr, there remains in their hearts a hesitation concerning the validity of their intention. And perhaps they are assailed by doubt in the takbīr itself, so that the very form of the takbīr becomes altered due to excessive caution, and they miss hearing the Fātiḥah. They do this at the beginning of the prayer, then they do it throughout the entire prayer — yet they do not stir their hearts, and they are deluded by it. They do not know that the presence of the heart in prayer is the obligatory duty. Satan merely deluded them and adorned it for them, saying to them: "By this caution you are distinguished from the common folk, and you are upon goodness with your Lord."

### | الفرقة الثالثة

مخارجها.. فلا تزال تحتاط فى التشديدات.. والفرق بين الضاد والظاء.. لا
يهمه غير ذلك ولا يتفكر فى أسرار الفاتحة ولا فى معانيها.. ولم يعلم أنه لم
يكلف الخلق فى تلاوة القرآن من تحقيق مخارج الحروف إلا ما جرت به عادتهم فى
الكلام..
وهذا غرور عظيم.. ومثالهم مثال من حمل رسالة إلى مجلس السلطان وأمر أن

مخارج الحروف ويكررها ويعيدها مرة بعد أخرى وهو مع ذلك غافل عن مقصود
الرسالة.. ومراعاة حرمة المجلس.. وبهذا يرد إلى دار المجانين ويحكم عليه
بفقد العقل.

اليوم والليلة ختما.. وألسنتهم تجرى به.. وقلوبهم تتردى فى أودية الأماني
والتفكر فى الدنيا.. ولا يتفكر فى معانى القرآن..لينزجر بزواجره.. ويتعظ
بمواعظه.. ويقف عند أوامره ونواهيه.. ويعتبر بمواضع الاعتبار  منه.. ويتلذذ
به من حيث المعنى لا من حيث النظم.. ومن قرأ كتاب الله تعالى فى اليوم
والليلة مائة مرة.. ثم ترك أوامره ونواهيه فهو مستحق العقوبة.. وربما قد
يكون له صوت لين فهو يقرأ ويتلذذ به.. ويغتر باستلذاذه.. ويظن أن ذلك
مناجاة الله سبحانه تعالى.. وسماع كلامه.. وهيهات ما أبعده.. إذا لذاته فى

### | الفرقة الخامسة

وفرقة أخرى اغتروا بالصوم.. وربما صاموا الدهر.. وصاموا الأيام الشريفة
وهم فيها لا يحفظون ألسنتهم من الغيبة.. ولا خواطرهم من الربا.. ولا بطونهم
من الحرام عند الافطار ولا من الهذيان
من أنواع الفضول.. وذلك غرور عظيم.. وهؤلاء تركوا الواجب.. وأبقوا

وفرقة أخرى أخذت فى طريق الخشية والأمر بالمعروف والنهى عن المنكر ينكر
على الناس.. ويأمرهم بالخير.. وينسى نفسه!.. وإذا أمرهم بالخير عنف وطلب
الرياسة والعزة.. وإذا باشر منكرا أنكر عليه.. وغضب وقال: أنا المحتسب..
فكيف تنكر على.. وقد تجمع الناس فى مجلسه أو مسجده.. ومن تأخر عنه أغلظ
عليه القول.. وإنما غرضه الرياء والسمعة وحب الرئاسة.. وعلامة أنه لو قام

بل منهم من يؤذن ويظن أنه يؤذن لله تعالى.. ولو جاء غيره وأذن فى وقت
غيبته قامت عليه القيامة.. وقال: لم أخذ حقى؟!.. وزوحمت؟!..
ومنهم من يتقيد أمام مسجد ويظن أنه على خير.. وإنما غرضه أن يقال: إنه

### | الفرقة السابعة

وفرقة أخرى جاوروا بمكة والمدينة واغتروا بهما.. ولم يراقبوا قلوبهم..
ولم يطهروا ظواهرهم وبواطنهم.. وربما كانت قلوبهم متعلقة ببلادهم.. وتراهم
يتحدثون بذلك.. ويقولون: جاورنا بمكة كذا كذا سنة.. وهم مغرورون لأن الأقوم
لهم أن يكونوا ببلدة وقلوبهم متعلقة بمكة.. وإن جاور أحدهم يجب عليه أن
يحفظ حق الجوار..  فإن جاور بمكة حفظ حق الله تعالى.. وإن جاور بالمدينة حفظ
حق النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم.. ومن يقدر على ذلك؟.. وهؤلاء مغرورون
بالظواهر.. وظنوا أن الحيطان تنجيهم.. وهيهات.. وربما لا تسمح نفسه بلقمة
يتصدق بها على فقير.. وما أصعب المجاورة فى حق الخلق.. فكيف بمجاورة
الخالق!.. وما أحسن مجاورته بحفظ جوارحه وقلبه..

- Root: و-س-و-س (waswasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The faint, subtle whisper that reaches the heart; obsessive prompting that distracts from sound intention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic idiom, the insinuation of Satan that veils the servant from the reality of worship (ʿibādah); here, a pathological scrupulosity (al-waswāsah) in ritual mechanics.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the whisper itself; metaphorical (majāz) — the obsessive fixation on letter-articulation to the exclusion of meaning, a displacement of the end by the means.
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deception, delusion, heedlessness of consequence; the state of one who is beguiled by appearances.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, al-ghurūr is reliance upon something that cannot avail — a false security before God, often rooted in self-amazement (ʿujb) or the devil's embellishment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the mirage (sarāb) that the thirsty take for water; metaphorical — every act of worship performed for other than God's countenance, whose outward form is sound but whose inward reality is void.
- Root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reckon, to suppose, to hold an opinion without verification.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The cognitive act of presumption (ḥusbān) that substitutes subjective estimation for certain knowledge (yaqīn) — the epistemic root of self-deception.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — arithmetic reckoning; metaphorical — the soul's false accounting of its own deeds, deeming that which is null as weighty.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — In the phrase "وهم فيها لا يحفظون ألسنتهم" (while they therein do not guard their tongues), the circumstantial clause (ḥāl) is a verbal sentence introduced by the particle "wa," denoting a simultaneous state that qualifies the agent's action, thereby exposing the contradiction between the outward act (fasting) and the inward condition (unrestrained tongue) — a syntactic mirror of the moral incongruity.
chapters.translation:
### | The Third Category

And another group — obsessive whisperings (al-waswāsah) overcame them concerning the articulation of the letters of the Fātiḥah and the rest of the invocations (al-adhkār) from their proper points of exit (makhārij). Thus they cease not to be over-scrupulous regarding the doubled consonants (al-tashdīdāt) and the distinction between ḍād and ẓāʾ. Nothing else concerns them, nor do they reflect upon the secrets of the Fātiḥah nor upon its meanings. And they know not that the creation were not charged, in the recitation of the Qur'an, with perfecting the articulation of letters save to the extent of their customary manner in speech.

And this is a mighty delusion (ghurūr ʿaẓīm). Their likeness is the likeness of one who carries a message to the court of the Sultan and is commanded to deliver it as it ought to be delivered. So he sets about delivering the message, refining the articulation of its letters, repeating and reiterating them time after time — while all the while he is heedless of the purport of the message and of observing the sanctity of the court. By this, he is returned to the house of the insane and judged to have lost his reason.

### | The Fourth Category

And another group were deluded by the recitation of the Qur'an — they squander it wantonly (yahdirūnahu hadran). Perhaps they complete the entire recitation (khatm) once in the day and the night, their tongues running along with it, while their hearts plunge into the valleys of vain fancies and reflection upon the world. They reflect not upon the meanings of the Qur'an, so as to be restrained by its prohibitions (zawājir), admonished by its exhortations (mawāʿiẓ), halted at its commands and interdictions, and take heed from its places of warning. Nor do they delight in it from the standpoint of meaning, but only from the standpoint of its arrangement (naẓm). And whosoever reads the Book of God — exalted be He — a hundred times in the day and the night, then abandons its commands and interdictions, he is deserving of punishment. And perhaps he may have a soft voice, so he recites and takes delight in it, and is deluded by his own delight, supposing that this is a private communion with God — exalted be He — and a hearing of His speech. How far! How very far is he! For his delight is in his own voice. Had he perceived the delight of God's speech, he would not have looked to his voice and its sweetness, nor would his mind have clung to it. And the delight of God's speech is only from the standpoint of meaning.

### | The Fifth Category

And another group were deluded by fasting — perhaps they fast perpetually (al-dahr), and fast the noble days — yet while therein they guard not their tongues from backbiting (al-ghībah), nor their thoughts from usury (al-ribā), nor their bellies from the unlawful at the breaking of the fast, nor from idle prattle of the various kinds of meddlesomeness. And that is a mighty delusion. These have abandoned the obligatory (al-wājib) and preserved the commendable (al-mandūb), supposing that they shall be saved. How far! Only he is saved who comes to God with a sound heart (qalb salīm).

### | The Sixth Category

And another group took to the path of fear (al-khashyah) and commanding the good and forbidding the evil — one of them denounces the people and commands them to goodness, and forgets his own soul! And when he commands them to good, he is harsh, and seeks leadership and honor. And when he himself commits a wrong, and someone denounces him for it, he becomes angry and says: "I am the muḥtasib — how dare you denounce me?!" And when people gather in his assembly or his mosque, and one lags behind him, he speaks harshly to him. Yet his aim is only ostentation (al-riyāʾ), reputation (al-sumʿah), and love of leadership. And the sign of this is that were another to lead in his mosque, he would be emboldened against him.

Nay, among them is one who gives the call to prayer (adhān), supposing that he calls for God — exalted be He — yet were another to come and give the call in his absence, the Day of Resurrection would be established for him, and he would say: "Why was my right taken? Why was I crowded out?!"

And among them is one who binds himself to the front of a mosque, supposing that he is upon good — yet his aim is only that it be said: "He is the imam of the mosque." And the sign of this is that were another put forward, even one more pious and more learned than he, it would weigh heavily upon him.

### | The Seventh Category

And another group took up residence (jāwarū) in Mecca and Medina and were deluded by them — they watched not over their hearts, nor purified their outward and inward states. Perhaps their hearts were attached to their own lands, and you see them speaking of that, saying: "We resided in Mecca for such-and-such years." And they are deluded, for the more upright thing for them would be to be in their own town while their hearts are attached to Mecca. And if one of them resides, he must observe the right of neighboring (ḥaqq al-jiwār). For if he resides in Mecca, he must observe the right of God — exalted be He — and if he resides in Medina, he must observe the right of the Prophet — peace be upon him. And who is able to do that? These are deluded by outward appearances, supposing that the walls will save them. How far! And perhaps his soul would not yield a single morsel to give in charity to a poor man. How difficult is neighboring in the case of creatures — how then with neighboring the Creator! And how excellent is His neighboring, by guarding one's limbs and one's heart.

### | الفرقة الثامنة

وفرقة أخرى زهدت فى المال وقنعت من الطعام واللباس بالدون.. ومن السكن
بالمساجد. وظنت أنها أدركت رتبة الزهاد.. وهم مع ذلك راغبون فى الرياسة
والجاه.. والزهادة إنما تحصل بأحد أشياء: إما بالتعلم أو بالوعظ.. أو بمجرد
الزهد.. فلقد تركوا أهون الأمرين.. وباءوا بأعظم المهلكات.. فإن الجاه أعظم
من المال.. ولو أخذ المال وترك الجاه.. كان إلى السلامة أقرب.. وهؤلاء
مغرورون بظنهم أنهم من الزهاد فى الدنيا.. ولم يفهموا كيف مكر بهم.. وربما
تقدم الأغنياء على الفقراء..
ومنهم من يعجب بعلمه.. ومنهم من يؤثر الخلوة وهو عن شروطها خال.. ومنهم
من يعطى المال فلا يأخذه خيفة أن يقال بطل زهده.. وهو راغب فى الدنيا..
خائف من ذم الناس.. ومنهم من شدد على نفسه فى أعمال الجوامع.. حتى يصلى فى
اليوم مثلا ألف ركعة ويختم القرآن وهو فى جميع ذلك لا يخطر له مراعاة القلب
وتفقده وتطهيره من الرياء والكبر والعجب وسائر المهلكات.. وربما يظن أن
العبادة الظاهرة ترجح بها كفة الحسنات.. وهيهات ذرة من ذى تقوى.. وخلق واحد
من خلق الأكياس أفضل من أمثال الجبال عملا بالجوارح.. ثم قد يغتر بقول من
يقول له: إنك من أوتاد الأرض.. وأولياء الله وأحبائه.. فيفرح لذلك.. ويطهر
له تزكية نفسه.. ولو شوتم يوما واحدا ثلاث مرات أو مرتين لكفر وجاهد من فعل
ذلك به.. وربما قال لمن سبه: لا يغفر الله لك أبدا..

### | الفرقة التاسعة

وفرقة أخرى حرصت على النوافل، ولم يعظم اعتدادها بالفرائض.. فتارة يفرح
بصلاة الضحى، وصلاة الليل.. وأمثال هذه النوافل، فلا يجد لصلاة الفريضة لذة
ولا خير من الله تعالى، لشدة حرصه على المبادرة فى أول  الوقت.. وينسى قوله
صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ما تقرب المتقربون بأفضل ما افترضه الله عليهم) .
وترك الترتيب بين الخيرات من جملة الغرور.. بل قد يتعين على الإنسان
فرضان: أحدهما يفوت والآخر لا يفوت.. أو نفلان أحدهما يضيق وقته والآخر
متسع وقته.. فإن لم يحفظ الترتيب كان مغرورا.. ونظائر ذلك أكثر من أن
تحصى.. فإن المعصية ظاهرة.. وإنما الغامض تقديم بعض الطاعات على بعض..
كتقديم الفرائض كلها على النوافل.. وتقديم فروض الأعيان على فروض الكفايات
التى لا قائم بها على ما قدم بها غيره.. وتقديم الأهم من فروض الأعيان على
ما دونه.. وتقديم ما يفوت مثل تقديم حق الوالدة على الوالد.. وتقديم الدين
على القروض غيره.. وما أعظم العبد أن ينفذ ذلك.. ويرتبه.. ولكن الغرور فى
الترتيب دقيق خفى لا يقدر عليه إلا العلماء الراسخون فى العلم رضى الله
عنهم وغفر لهم.

### | الصنف الثالث

### | من المغرورين أرباب الأموال وفرقهم

### | الفرقة الأولى

فرقة منهم يحرصون على بناء المساجد والمدارس والرباطات والصهاريج للماء..
وما يظهر للناس.. ويكتبون أسماءهم بالآجر عليه.. ليتخلده ذكرهم، ويبقى بعد

- Root: ز-ه-د (z-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Abstinence, renunciation; choosing the lesser of worldly goods; contentment with the bare minimum.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Asceticism as a virtue of the heart—detachment from worldly allurements, not merely outward paucity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in renouncing possessions; metaphorical (majāz) when claimed by one whose heart clings to status.
- Root: ر-ي-س (r-y-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Leadership, headship; being foremost in command.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Craving for precedence over others—a hidden idol of the soul, more perilous than wealth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in political office; metaphorical for any dominance over hearts, including scholarly fame.
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deception, delusion; being beguiled by appearances.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Self-deception wherein one mistakes a lesser good for the greater, or vice versa.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in being tricked by another; metaphorical in the soul's self-beguilement.
- Root: ت-ر-ت-ي-ب (t-r-t-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ordering, arranging sequentially.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The proper hierarchy of religious obligations—prioritizing the obligatory over the supererogatory.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in physical sequence; metaphorical in moral precedence.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — When multiple clauses are joined by "wa" (and), each retains its independent syntactic force, yet the sequence implies a logical or temporal ordering, as in "تركوا أهون الأمرين وباءوا بأعظم المهلكات" (they abandoned the easier of two matters and returned laden with the greatest of destructions).
chapters.translation:
### | The Eighth Group

And another group renounced wealth and were content with the meanest of food and clothing, and with mosques as dwellings. They fancied that they had attained the rank of the ascetics (zuhhād). Yet, for all that, they were desirous of leadership (riyāsah) and status (jāh). But asceticism (zuhd) is only realized through one of three things: either through learning, or through preaching, or through sheer renunciation. So they abandoned the easier of the two matters and returned laden with the greatest of destructions—for status is greater than wealth. Had they taken wealth and left status, they would have been nearer to safety. These are deluded by their presumption that they are among the ascetics of this world, and they did not understand how they were deceived. And perhaps the rich are given precedence over the poor.

Among them is one who marvels at his own knowledge; and among them is one who prefers seclusion (khalwah) while being empty of its conditions; and among them is one who is given wealth but refuses to take it, fearing that it be said his asceticism is void—while he is desirous of this world, fearful of people's blame. And among them is one who imposes hardship upon himself in the works of the congregational mosques, such that he prays, for example, a thousand rakʿahs in a day and completes the Quran—yet throughout all of that, it never occurs to him to watch over his heart, to inspect it, and to purify it from ostentation (riyāʾ), pride (kibr), self-admiration (ʿujb), and the rest of the destructive vices (muhlikāt). Perhaps he even supposes that outward worship tips the scale of good deeds. But far from it! A single atom of a God-fearing man, and a single trait of the prudent, is better than mountains upon mountains of bodily works. Then he may be deluded by the saying of one who tells him: "You are among the pegs (awtād) of the earth, and among the friends of God (awliyāʾ Allāh) and His beloved ones." So he rejoices at that, and self-purification (tazkiyah) becomes manifest to him. Yet were he reviled but once, three times or twice, he would disbelieve and strive against the one who did that to him. And perhaps he says to the one who insulted him: "May God never forgive you, ever."

### | The Ninth Group

And another group was eager for supererogatory acts (nawāfil), yet did not hold the obligatory acts (farāʾiḍ) in great esteem. So at times one of them rejoices in the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā) and the night prayer, and the like of these supererogatory acts—yet he finds no delight in the obligatory prayer, nor any good from God—may He be exalted—due to his intense eagerness to hasten at the first moment of the time. And he forgets his saying—peace and blessings be upon him: {«ما تقرب المتقربون بأفضل ما افترضه الله عليهم»} ("The seekers of nearness have not drawn near to God with anything better than what He has made obligatory upon them"). And neglecting the proper ordering (tartīb) among good deeds is part of delusion (ghurūr). Indeed, a person may have two obligatory duties incumbent upon him: one that lapses and one that does not lapse—or two supererogatory acts, one whose time is constricted and the other whose time is expansive. If he does not preserve the ordering, he is deluded. And the parallels to this are more numerous than can be counted. For disobedience (maʿṣiyah) is apparent; rather, the obscure matter is the precedence of some acts of obedience over others—such as giving all obligatory acts precedence over supererogatory ones; and giving the individual obligations (furūḍ al-ʿayn) precedence over the communal obligations (furūḍ al-kifāyāt) when no one else has undertaken them as others have; and giving the more important of the individual obligations precedence over what is lesser; and giving precedence to what lapses—such as giving the right of the mother precedence over the father; and giving the repayment of debt precedence over loans to others. How great is the servant who executes this and arranges it! But the delusion in ordering is subtle and hidden, which none can grasp except the deeply rooted scholars (al-rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm)—may God be pleased with them and forgive them.

### | The Third Class

### | Of the Deluded: The Possessors of Wealth and Their Groups

### | The First Group

A group among them are eager to build mosques, schools (madāris), hospices (ribāṭāt), and cisterns for water—and whatever is visible to people—and they inscribe their names upon them in brick, so that their remembrance be perpetuated and their trace remain after death. And they suppose that they have thereby merited forgiveness. Yet they have been deluded in this from two aspects.

The first: that they have acquired these [funds] through injustice, dubious means (shubuhāt), bribes (rishā), and prohibited channels. And they have exposed themselves to God's wrath in earning them. So they have disobeyed God in their acquisition. Thus, what is incumbent upon them in repentance is to return them to their owners if they are alive, or to their heirs. And if none of them remains and they have become extinct, then the obligation is to expend them in the most important of public interests (maṣāliḥ). And perhaps the most important is the distribution to the poor. And what benefit is there in a building that one dispenses with, abandons, and then dies? Rather, what has overcome these people is ostentation (riyāʾ), fame, and the pleasure of being mentioned.

And the second aspect: that they suppose themselves to possess sincerity (ikhlāṣ) and the intention of good in spending and in raising lofty structures. Yet were one of them asked to spend a single dinar upon a poor man, his soul would not permit him that—because the love of praise is concealed within his innermost being.

### | الفرقة الثانية

وفرقة أخرى ربما اكتسبوا الحلال.. واجتنبوا الحرام وأنفقوه على المساجد،
وهى أيضا مغرورة من وجهين: أحدهما: الرياء وطلب السمعة والثناء.. فإنه ربما
يكون فى  جواره أو بلده فقراء، وصرف المال إليهم أهم.. فإن المساجد كثيرة
والغرض منها الجامع وحده فيجزئ عن غيره.. وليس الغرض بناء المسجد فى كل سكة
وفى كل درب والمساكين والفقراء محتاجون.
وإنما خف عليهم دفع المال فى بناء المساجد لظهور ذلك بين الناس.. ولما
يسمع من الثناء عليه من الخلق، فيظن أنه يعمل لله وهو يعمل لغير الله..
والله أعلم بذلك.. وإنما نيته عليه غضب.. وإنما قال: قصدت أنه لله تعالى.
والثانى: أنه يصرف ذلك فى زخرفة المساجد وتزيينها بالنقوش المنهى عنها..
الشاغلة قلوب المصلين لأنهم ينظرون إليها وتشغلهم عن الخشوع فى الصلاة..
وعن حضور القلب.. وهو المقصود..
وكلما طرأ على المصلين فى صلاتهم وفى غير صلاتهم فهو فى رقبة البانى
للمسجد.. إذ لا يحل تزيين المسجد بوجه..
قال الحسن رضى الله عنه: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أراد أن
يبنى مسجده بالمدينة أتاه جبريل فقال له: (ابنه سبعة أذرع طولا فى السماء
لا تزخرفه ولا تنقشه) .
وغرور هؤلاء أنهم رأوا المنكر معروفا فاتكلوا عليه.

### | الفرقة الثالثة

وفرقة أخرى ينفقون الأموال فى الصدقات على الفقراء والمساكين.. ويطلبون
بها المحافل الجامعة.. ومن الفقراء من عادته الشكر..والإفشاء للمعروف..
ويكرهون التصدق فى السر.. ويرون إخفاء الصدقة للفقير لما يأخذه منهم خيانة
عليهم.. وكفرانا..وربما تركوا جيرانهم جائعين.. ولذلك قال ابن عباس رضى
الله عنهما: (فى آخر الزمان يكثر الحاج بلا سبب.. يهوى لهم السفر.. ويبسط
لهم فى الرزق ويرجعون مجرمين مسلوبين.. يهوى بأحدهم بعيره بين القفار
والرمال.. وجاره مأسور إلى جنبه فلا يواسيه.. ولا يتفقده) ..

### | الفرقة الرابعة

وفرقة أخرى من أرباب الأموال.. يحفظون الأموال.. ويمسكونها بحكم البخل
ويشتغلون بالعبادات الدينية التى لا يحتاجون فيها إلى نفقة.. كصيام
النهار.. وقيام الليل.. وختم القرآن.. وهؤلاء مغرورن.. لأن البخل المهلك قد
استولى على باطنهم.. فهم
محتاجون إلى قمعه بإخراج المال.. فاشتغلوا بطلب فضائل وهم مشتغلون عنها..
ومثالهم مثال من دخلت فى ثوبه حية.. وقد أشرف على الهلاك.. وهم مشغول عنها
بطلب السكنجبين ليسكن به  الصفراء.. ومن لدغته الحية كيف يحتاج إلى ذلك؟!..
ولذلك قيل لبشر الحافى: إن فلانا كثير الصوم والصلاة.. فقال: المسكين ترك
حاله.. ودخل فى حال غيره.. وإنما حال هذا إطعام الطعام للجائع.. والإنفاق
على المساكين.. فهو أفضل له من تجويع نفسه.. ومن صلاته.. مع جمعه للدنيا
ومنعه للفقراء..

### | الفرقة الخامسة

وفرقة أخرى غلب عليهم البخل.. فلا تسمح نفوسهم إلا بأداء الزكاة فقط.. ثم
إنهم يخرجونها من المال الخبيث الردئ الذى يرغبون عن.. ويطلبون من الفقراء
من يخدمهم.. ويتردد فى حاجاتهم.. أو من يحتاج إليه فى المستقبل للاستئجار
لهم فى الخدمة.. ومن لهم فيه غرض.. ويسلمونها إلى شخص بعينه واحد من
الكبار.. ممن
يستظهر بخشيته.. لينال بذلك عنده منزلة.. فيقوم بحاجته.. وكل ذلك مفسد
للنية.. ومحبط للعمل.. وصاحبه مغرور.. يظن أنه مطيع لله تعالى.. وهو فاجر..
إذا يطلب بعبادة الله تعالى عوضا من غيره.. فهذا وغيره وأمثاله مغرورون
بالأموال..

### | الفرقة السادسة

وفرقة أخرى من عوام الخلق وأرباب والأموال والفقراء.. اغتروا بحضور مجالس
الذكر.. واعتقدوا أن ذلك يغنيهم ويكفيهم.. فاتخذوا ذلك عادة ويظنون أن لهم
على مجرد سماع الوعظ دون العمل.. ودون الاتعاظ أجرا.. وهم مغرورن لأن فضل
مجالس الذكر لكونها رغبة فى الخير.. وإذا لم تهج الرغبة فلا خير فيها..
والرغبة محمودة.. لأنها تبعث على العمل.. وإن لم تبعث على العمل فلا خير
فيها.. وربما يغتر بما يسمعه من الوعظ.. وإنما يداخله رقه كرقة النساء
فيبكى!.. وربما يسمع كلاما مخوفا فلا يزال يصفر بين يديه ويقول: يا سلام
سلم!.. ونعوذ بالله!.. والحمد لله.. وحسبى الله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا
بالله!.. ويظن أنه قد أتى بالخير كله.. وهو مغرور.. ومثاله مثال المريض..
الذى يحضر إلى مجالس الأطباء.. ويسمع ما يصفونه من الأدوية ولا يعقلها..
ولا يشتغل بها ويظن أنه يجد الراحة بذلك. والجائع الذى يحضر عنده من يصف له
الأطعمة اللذيذة..
فكل وعظ لا يغير منك صفة تغير بدونها أفعالك.. حتى تقبل على الله وتعرض
عن الدنيا.. وتقبل إقبالا قويا.. وإن لم  تفعل فذلك الوعظ زيادة حجة عليك..
فإذا رأيته وسيلة لك كنت مغرورا.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ ر ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "heedlessness" or "being deceived by appearances" — a state where one is lulled into false security by a mirage-like semblance of good.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, it is the self-deception (ightirār) of one who relies on outward acts while neglecting inward sincerity (ikhlāṣ) and the heart's presence (ḥuḍūr al-qalb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it refers to being duped by a glittering surface (majāz of the world's allure); here, it is metaphorical — the delusion of assuming divine acceptance without fulfilling the true conditions of worship.
- Root: ر ي ء (r-y-')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Show" or "ostentation" — performing acts for the gaze of others.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Riyaʾ is the hidden shirk of intention, nullifying the act's value before God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Contrasts ḥaqīqah (sincere act for God alone) with majāz (act directed to creatures).
- Root: خ ش ع (kh-sh-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Humility, submissiveness, and stillness of the limbs and heart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The essence of prayer's validity — the heart's presence before God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical lowering; metaphorical for the soul's awe.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The repeated "وفرقة أخرى" (and another group) functions as a series of coordinated nominal sentences, each introducing a distinct category, with the predicate carrying the semantic weight of delusion (maghrūrūn). The conditional clauses (e.g., "إذا لم تهج الرغبة") follow the standard law of conditionality, where the protasis governs the apodosis.
chapters.translation:
### | The Second Group

And another group — perhaps they earn what is lawful, and avoid what is unlawful, and spend it upon mosques. Yet they too are deluded in two respects: The first is ostentation (al-riyāʾ), seeking reputation and praise. For perhaps in their vicinity or their town there are poor people, and directing the wealth to them would be more important. For mosques are many, and the purpose of them is fulfilled by the congregational mosque alone, which suffices in place of others. And the purpose is not to build a mosque in every alley and every lane, while the destitute and the poor are in need.

And the only reason spending money on building mosques is easy for them is its visibility among the people, and the praise they hear from the creatures upon it. So he thinks he is working for God, while he is working for other than God — and God knows best of that. And his intention therein is only wrath. And he merely says: "I intended it for God the Exalted."

The second: that he spends it on ornamenting mosques and adorning them with the engravings that are prohibited — those which distract the hearts of the worshippers, for they gaze upon them, and they divert them from humility (al-khushūʿ) in prayer, and from the heart's presence — which is the very purpose. And every distraction that befalls the worshippers in their prayer and outside their prayer is upon the neck of the mosque's builder, for it is not lawful to adorn a mosque in any manner.

Al-Ḥasan (may God be pleased with him) said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) intended to build his mosque in Medina, Gabriel came to him and said to him: {«Build it seven cubits in height toward the sky — do not ornament it, and do not engrave it.»}

And the delusion of these is that they saw the reprehensible as commendable, and so they relied upon it.

### | The Third Group

And another group spends wealth in alms upon the poor and the destitute, and seeks thereby the gatherings that assemble [people]. And among the poor are those whose habit is gratitude and the spreading abroad of the good deed. And they dislike giving charity in secret, and they see the concealment of charity from the poor — because of what the poor takes from them — as treachery against them and ingratitude. And perhaps they leave their own neighbors hungry. For that reason, Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: {«In the end of time, the pilgrims will multiply without cause — travel will be made easy for them, and provision will be spread for them, and they will return as criminals, despoiled. One of them will have his camel stray between the deserts and the sands, while his neighbor is imprisoned beside him — he neither relieves him nor checks on him.»}

### | The Fourth Group

And another group among the owners of wealth — they guard their wealth and withhold it by the rule of miserliness, and they occupy themselves with religious devotions that require no expenditure, such as fasting the day, praying the night, and completing the Qurʾān. These are deluded, because destructive miserliness has seized their inner selves. They are in need of suppressing it by expending wealth. Yet they occupy themselves with seeking virtues while they are diverted from them. Their example is the example of one into whose garment a snake has entered, and he is on the verge of destruction — yet he is occupied away from it with seeking oxymel (sikanjabīn) to calm his yellow bile. And how does one bitten by a snake need that?!

For that reason, it was said to Bishr al-Ḥāfī: "So-and-so is abundant in fasting and prayer." He said: "The poor wretch has abandoned his own state and entered into the state of another. For the state of this one is feeding food to the hungry and spending upon the destitute — that is better for him than starving himself, and than his prayer, while he amasses the world and withholds it from the poor."

### | The Fifth Group

And another group — miserliness has overcome them, so their souls do not permit anything except the payment of the zakāh alone. Then they extract it from the vile, inferior wealth that they themselves disdain. And they seek from the poor those who will serve them and go back and forth in their needs, or those who will be needed in the future for hiring in service, or those in whom they have an interest. And they hand it over to a specific person, one of the notables, one whose fear they seek to exploit, so that they may attain a station with him thereby, and he may fulfill their need. And all of that corrupts the intention and nullifies the deed. And its doer is deluded — he thinks he is obedient to God the Exalted, while he is a profligate (fājir), for he seeks, through the worship of God, a recompense from other than Him. So this one, and others, and their likes, are deluded by wealth.

### | The Sixth Group

And another group among the common folk, the owners of wealth, and the poor — they are deluded by attending the gatherings of remembrance (majālis al-dhikr), and they believe that this suffices them and spares them [from further obligation]. So they take it as a habit, and they think that for merely hearing the admonition — without acting, and without being moved to heed — they have a reward. And they are deluded, for the virtue of remembrance gatherings lies in their being a desire for good. And when the desire is not stirred, there is no good in them. And the desire is praiseworthy because it impels one to action. And if it does not impel one to action, there is no good in it.

And perhaps one is deluded by what he hears of the admonition — and only a softness enters him, like the softness of women, and he weeps! And perhaps he hears terrifying speech, and he keeps whistling before it, saying: "O Peace, grant peace! And we seek refuge in God! And praise be to God! And God suffices me, and there is no might and no power except through God!" — and he thinks he has brought all good. And he is deluded. His example is the example of the sick man who attends the gatherings of physicians and hears what they prescribe of medicines, but does not comprehend them, nor occupy himself with them, and thinks he will find relief thereby. And the hungry man who has someone beside him describing delicious foods.

So every admonition that does not change in you a quality, without which your deeds would not change — until you turn to God and turn away from the world, and turn with a strong turning — and if you do not do so, then that admonition is an added argument against you. So if you see it as a means for you, you are deluded.

### | The Fourth Class

### | Of the Deluded: The Sufis

And how overwhelming is delusion upon these deluded ones!!

من الآثار الخفية والجلية.. وكل ذلك من منازل

ويتنافسون فى الرغيف.. والفلس والحبة.. ويتحاسدون على النقير
والقطمير..ويمزق بعضهم أعراض بعض مهما خالفه فى شئ من غرضه.. وهؤلاء
مغرورن.. ومثالهم مثال عجوز سمعت أن الشجعان والأبطال والمقاتلين ثبتت
أسماؤهم فى الديوان فتزيت بزيهم.. ووصلت إلى الملك.. فعرضت على ميزان
العرض. فوجدت عجوز سوء.. فقيل لها: أما تستحين فى استهتارك بالملك؟!
اطرحوها حول الفيل.. فطرحوها حول الفيل فركضها.. حتى ماتت..

### | الفرقة الثانية

وفرقة أخرى ازدادت على هؤلاء فى الغرور.. إذا صعب عليها الاقتداء فى
بذاذة الثياب.. والرضا بالدون فى المطعم والمنكح والمسكن.. وأرادت أن
تتظاهر بالتصوف.. ولم تجد بدا من التزيى بزيهم.. فتركت الخز والإبريسم..
وطلبت المرقعات النفسية..
والفوط الرقيقة.. والسجادة المصبوغة.. وقيمتها أكثر من قيمة الخز
والإبريسم.. ولا يجتنبون معصية ظاهرة.. فكيف باطنه.. وإنما غرضهم رغد
العيش.. وأكل أموال السلاطين.. وهم مع ذلك يظنون بأنفسهم الخير.. وضرر
هؤلاء أشد من ضرر اللصوص.. لأن هؤلاء يسرقون القلوب بالزى.. ويقتدى بهم
الغير.. فيكون بسبب هلاكهم.. وإن اطلع على فضائحهم ربما ظن أهل التصوف
كذلك.. فيصرح بذم الصوفية على الإطلاق..

### | الفرقة الثالثة

وفرقة أخرى ادعت علم المكاشفة.. ومشاهدة الحق.. ومجاوزة المقامات..
والوصول والملازمة فى عين الشهود..
والوصول إلى القرب.. ولا يعرف ذلك.. ولا وصل إليه باللفظ والإثم..  ويلفق
من الألفاظ الطامة كلمات.. فهو يردها.. ويعلن أن ذلك أعلى من علم الأولين
والآخرين.. وهو ينظر إلى الفقراء والمقرئين.. والمفسرين والمحدثين.. وأصناف
العلماء بعين الازدراء فضلا عن العوام.. حتى أن الفلاح ليترك فلاحته.
والحايك حياكته.. ويلازمهم أياما معدودة.. ويتلقف تلك الكلمات الزائفة..
فتراه يرددها كأنه يتكلم عن الوحى.. ويخبر عن أسرار الأسرار ويستحقر بذلك
جميع العباد والعلماء.. فيقول فى العباد: أجراء متعبدون.. ويقول فى
العلماء: إنهم بالحديث محجوبون.. ويدعى لنفسه أنه الواصل إلى الحق.. وأنه
من المقربين.. وهو عند الله من الفجار المنافقين.. وعند أرباب القلوب من
الحمقى الجاهلين.. لم يحكم قط علما.. ولا يهذب خلقا.. ولا يراقب قلبا سوى
اتباع الهوى.. وتلفيق الهذيانات.. ولو اشتغلوا بما ينفعهم كان أحسن لهم..

### | الفرقة الرابعة

وفرقة أخرى جاورت هؤلاء فأحسنت الأعمال.. وطلبت الحلال.. واشتغلت بتفقد
القلب.. وصار أحدهم يدعى المقامات من الزهد.. والتوكل.. والرضا.. والحب من
غير وقوف على حقيقة هذه المقامات وشروطها وعلاماتها وآفاتها..
فمنهم من يدعى الوجد وحب الله تعالى.. ويزعم أنه واله بالله تعالى..
ولعله قد يتخيل بالله تعالى خيالات فاسدة هى بدعة وكفر.. فيدعى حب الله
تعالى وقيل معرفته.. وذلك لا يتصور قط.. ثم إنه لا يخلو من مفارقة ما يكره
الله تعالى.. وإيثار هوى نفسه على أمر الله تعالى.. وعن ترك الأمور حياء من
الخلق.. ولو خلا ما تركها حياء من الله تعالى.. وليس يدرى أن كل ذلك يناقض
الحب.. وبعضهم ربما يميل إلى القناعة والتوكل فيخوض البوادى من غير زاد
ليصحح التوكل.. وليس يدرى أن ذلك بدعة لم تنقل عن السلف والصحافة رضى الله
عنهم أجمعين.. وقد كانوا أعرف بالتوكل منه.. وما فهموا من التوكل المخاطرة
بالروح وترك الزاد.. بل كانوا يأخذون الزاد وهم متوكلون على الله تعالى على
لا الزاد.. وهذا ربما يترك الزاد وهو متوكل على سبب من الأسباب واتقى به..
وما مقام من المقامات المنجية إلا وفيها غرور.. وقد اعتبرها قوم.. وقد
ذكرنا مداخل الآفات فيها ربع المنجيات فى الإحياء.

### | الفرقة الخامسة

وفرقة أخرى ضيقت على أنفسها أمر القوت حتى طلبت منه الحلال الخالص..
وأهملت تفقد القلب والجوارح فى غير هذه الخصلة الواحدة.. ومنهم من أهمل
الحلال فى مطعمه وملبسه ومكسبه فيتعمق
فى ذلك.. ولم يدر المسكين أن الله تعالى لم يرض من العباد إلا بالكمال فى
الطاعات، فمن اتبع البعض وأهل البعض فهو مغرور.

- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "delusion" (ghurūr) — being deceived by appearances, as in the glitter of the world (ghirrah) that veils one from reality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance — the state of one who relies on a false hope (rajāʾ) or outward semblance without the inward reality, akin to the Quranic warning against being deluded by the life of this world.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes the deception of a mirage (sarāb); metaphorically, it applies to those who mistake outward forms (zīy) for spiritual substance.
- Root: ز-ي-ي (z-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Attire" or "garb" (zīy) — the external dress and appearance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In spiritual contexts, zīy signifies the outward mark of a group, which may be adopted without the inner reality it symbolizes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for clothing; metaphorical for assuming the mannerisms and forms of a people without their essence.
- Root: م-ك-ش-ف (m-k-sh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Unveiling" (mukāshafah) — the removal of a covering to reveal what is hidden.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for direct, unveiled knowledge of divine realities granted to the saints (awliyāʾ), distinct from acquired knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for uncovering; in Sufi idiom, it denotes the inner vision of the heart, which cannot be claimed by mere words.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) and Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — The text employs extensive coordination (wa) to enumerate the deluded traits, and circumstantial clauses (ḥāl) to depict the state of the deluded (e.g., "with head bowed," "with sighs"), requiring careful parsing to preserve the cumulative rhetorical effect.

---

### | The First Group

Among them are the pseudo-Sufis of this age — save those whom God has protected. They are deluded by the garb, the speech, and the awe-inspiring bearing. They imitate the truthful Sufis in their dress, their appearance, their utterances, their courtesies, their rituals, their technical jargon, and their outward displays of wealth in the listening to music (samāʿ), the dancing, the purification, the prayer, and the sitting upon the prayer-rug with head bowed and tucked into the collar like one deep in thought, and in the sighs of breath, and in the lowering of the voice in conversation, and in the shouting — and so forth. When they have learned all this, they imagine that it will deliver them. Yet they have never once wearied themselves with spiritual striving (mujāhadah), self-discipline (riyāḍah), or vigilance over the heart in purifying the inner and the outer from hidden and manifest impurities. And all of that [striving] is among the stations of the Sufis. Then, moreover, they scramble greedily after the forbidden and the ambiguous (shubuhāt), and the wealth of the sultans. They vie with one another for the loaf, the coin, and the grain. They envy one another over the pittance of a date-stone (naqīr) and the husk of a seed (qaṭmīr). They tear apart one another's reputations whenever one opposes another in any matter of his desire. These are the deluded. Their likeness is that of an old woman who heard that the brave, the heroes, and the warriors had their names registered in the royal register (dīwān). So she donned their garb and came to the king. She was presented to the scale of inspection, and was found to be a wretched old woman. It was said to her: "Have you no shame in your reckless mockery of the king? Cast her before the elephant!" So they cast her before the elephant, and it trampled her until she died.

### | The Second Group

Another group increased in delusion beyond these. When it became difficult for them to imitate [the Sufis] in the coarseness of garments, and in being content with the meanest in food, marriage, and dwelling, and they desired to make a show of Sufism — yet found no way but to adopt their garb — they abandoned silk and brocade, and sought out patched cloaks (muraqqaʿāt) of fine quality, and delicate towels, and dyed prayer-rugs, the value of which exceeds that of silk and brocade. They do not avoid an open act of disobedience — how then the hidden one? Their sole aim is the ease of life and the devouring of the sultans' wealth. Yet for all that, they think well of themselves. The harm of these is greater than the harm of thieves, for these steal hearts by their garb, and others follow their example, and so are destroyed because of them. And if their scandals become known, perhaps the people of Sufism will be thought to be the same, and thus one will openly censure the Sufis without distinction.

### | The Third Group

Another group claimed the science of unveiling (mukāshafah), the witnessing of the Truth, the transcendence of the stations, the arrival and the permanence in the very eye of contemplation (ʿayn al-shuhūd), and the attainment of proximity [to God] — yet they know not that, nor have they arrived at it by word and sin. One of them fabricates words from grandiloquent phrases, and he repeats them, and proclaims that this is higher than the knowledge of the first and the last. He looks upon the poor, the Qurʾān-reciters, the exegetes, the traditionists, and all classes of scholars with an eye of contempt — let alone the common folk. So much so that the farmer abandons his farming, and the weaver his weaving, and attaches himself to them for a few days, and snatches up those false words. You see him repeating them as though he spoke from revelation, and he reports of the secrets of secrets, and holds in contempt thereby all the worshippers and the scholars. He says of the worshippers: "They are hired laborers, merely devoted to worship." And he says of the scholars: "They are veiled by hadith." And he claims for himself that he is the one who has arrived at the Truth, and that he is among those brought near — while in the sight of God he is among the wicked hypocrites, and in the sight of the masters of hearts he is among the foolish ignoramuses. He has never mastered any knowledge, nor refined any character, nor watched over any heart — nothing but the following of caprice and the patching together of delirious ravings. Had they occupied themselves with what would benefit them, it would have been better for them.

### | The Fourth Group

Another group drew near to these [in rank] but improved their deeds. They sought the lawful, and occupied themselves with the scrutiny of the heart. Yet one of them came to claim the stations — of asceticism (zuhd), trust in God (tawakkul), contentment (riḍā), and love (maḥabbah) — without pausing upon the reality of these stations, their conditions, their signs, and their afflictions. Among them is one who claims ecstasy (wajd) and the love of God Most High, and asserts that he is enamored of God Most High. Perhaps he even conceives of God Most High corrupt imaginings that are innovation (bidʿah) and unbelief (kufr). So he claims the love of God Most High, and it is said, His knowledge — yet that is never truly conceived. Then, moreover, he is not free from departing from what God dislikes, and preferring his own caprice over the command of God Most High, and abandoning things out of shame before creatures — for were he alone, he would not abandon them out of shame before God Most High. And he does not know that all of that contradicts love. And some of them perhaps incline to contentment and trust, and plunge into the deserts without provision in order to validate trust — yet he does not know that this is an innovation not transmitted from the Salaf and the Companions, may God be pleased with them all. They were more knowledgeable of trust than he. They did not understand trust to mean risking the soul and abandoning provision. Rather, they took provision while trusting in God Most High — not in the provision. And this one perhaps abandons provision while trusting in some [other] means and relying upon it. There is no station among the saving stations but that it contains a delusion. Some people have considered them [all], and we have mentioned the entry-points of their afflictions in the "Quarter of the Deliverers" (rubʿ al-munjiyāt) in the Iḥyāʾ.

### | The Fifth Group

Another group narrowed upon themselves the matter of sustenance until they sought from it the purely lawful, and neglected the scrutiny of the heart and the limbs in anything other than this single trait. And among them is one who neglects the lawful in his food, his clothing, and his earning, and goes to extremes in that — and the poor wretch does not know that God Most High has not required of His servants anything less than perfection in acts of obedience. Whoever follows some parts and neglects others is deluded.

### | الفرقة السادسة

وفرقة أخرى ادعت حسن الخلق والتواضع والسماحة. وقصدوا الخدمة للصوفية..
فجمعوا قوما وتكلفوا خدمتهم.. واتخذوا ذلك شبكة لحطام الدنيا.. وجمعا
للمال.. وإنما غرضهم التكثير، والتكبير.. وهم يظهرون أن غرضهم الخدمة
والتبعية.. ثم إنهم يجمعون من الحرام والشبهات لينفقوا عليهم.. ليكثر
أتباعهم.. وينشر بالخدمة اسمهم.. وبعضهم يأخذ من أموال السلطان وينفق
عليهم.. وبعضهم يأخذها لينفق فى طريق الحج على الصوفية.. ويزعم أن غرضهم
البر والإنفاق.. وباعث جميعهم الرياء والسمعة.. وذلك بإهمالهم لجميع أوامر
الله تعالى ظاهرا.. ورضاهم بأخذ الحرام والإنفاق منه.. ومثال ذلك: كالذى
ينفق ماله فى طريق الحاج.. وكمن يعمر مسجد الله تعالى ويطينه بالعذرة ويزعم
أن قصده العمارة..

### | الفرقة السابعة

وفرقة أخرى اشتغلت بالمجاهدة وتهذيب الأخلاق.. وتطهير النفس من عيوبها..
وصاروا يتعمقون فيها.. فاتخذوا البحث عن عيوب النفس ومعرفة خداعها علما
وحرفة لهم.. فهم فى جميع
الأحوال يشتغلون بالفحص عن عيوب النفس.. واستنباط دقيق الكلام فى
آفاتها.. فيقولون: هذا فى النفس عيب.. والغفلة فى كونه عيبا عيب.. ويشتغلون
فيها بكلمات متلبسة.. وضيعوا فى ذلك أوقاتهم.. وكأنهم وقفوا مع أنفسهم..
ولم يشتغلوا بخالقهم.. فمثالهم مثال من اشتغل بأوقات الحج وعوائقه.. ولم
يسلك طريق الحج.. وذلك لم يغنه عن الحج..

### | الفرقة الثامنة

وفرقة أخرى جاوزت هذه المرتبة.. وابتدأوا سلوك الطريق.. وانفتحت لهم
أبواب المعرفة.. فكلما شموا من مبادئ المعرفة رائحة تعجبوا منها.. وفرحوا
بها.. وأعجبهم غراسها.. فتعلقت قلوبهم بالالتفات إليها.. والتفكر فيها..
وفى كيفية انفتاح بابها عليهم.. واشتدادها على غيرهم.. وكل ذلك غرور.. لأن
عجائب طريق الله تعالى ليس لها نهاية.. فمن وقف مع كل أعجوبة.. وتقيد بها
قصرت خطاه.. وحرم الوصول إلى المقصد.. ومثاله مثال  من قدم على ملك.. فرأى
باب ميدانه روضة فيها أزهار وأنوار.. ولم يكن قد رآها قبل ذلك.. ولا رأى
مثلها.. فوقف ينظر إليها حتى فاته الوقت الذى يمكنه اللقاء بالملك فانصرف
خائبا.

### | الفرقة التاسعة

وفرقة أخرى جاوزت هؤلاء.. ولم تلتفت إلى ما يفيض عليهم من الأنوار فى
الطريق.. ولا إلى ما تيسر لهم من العطايا الجزيلة.. ولم يلتفتوا إليها..
ولا عرجوا عليها.. جادين فى السير.. فلما قاربوا الوصول ظنوا أنهم وصلوا..
فوقفوا.. ولم يتعدوا ذلك.. وغلطوا.. فإن لله سبعين حجابا من نور وظلمة..
ولا يصل السالك إلى حجاب من تلك الحجب إلا ويظن أنه قد وصل.. وإليه الإشارة
بقوله تعالى إخبار عن إبراهيم عليه أفضل الصلاة والسلام إذ قال: (فلما جن
عليه الليل رأى كوكبا) الآية.. وما أكثر الحجب فى هذا المقام.
فأول حجاب بين العبد وربه نفسه.. فإنه أمر ربانى عظيم.. وهو نور من أنوار
الله تعالى.. أعنى سر القلب الذى سيجلى حقيقة الحق كما هو حتى أنه يسمع
جملة العالم كله.. ويحيط به صور الورى.. فعند ذلك سيشرق نوره إشراقا
عظيما.. إذ يظهر فيه الوجود كله على ما هو عليه.. وهو فى أول الأمر محجوب
بمشكاة هى الساترة له.. فإذا تجلى نوره وانكشف جمال القلب بعد إشراق نور
الله تعالى عليه..
ربما التفت صاحب القلب إلى القلب.. فرأى من جماله الفائق ما يدهشه..
فربما صرح وقال: أنا الحق.. فإن لم يتضح ما وراء ذلك.. ووقف عنك هلك..
وبهذه العين نظر النصارى إلى المسيح عليه الصلاة والسلام.. لما رأوا من
إشراق نور الله تعالى عليه..
فغلطوا.. كمن رأى كوكبا فى مرآة.. أو فى ماء.. فيظن أن الكواكب المرآة..
فيمد يده ليأخذه.. فهو مغرور..

### | هل هناك أنواع أخرى فى طريق السلوك

وأنواع الغرور فى طريق السلوك إلى الله..لا تستقصى إلا بعد شرح جميع
العلوم الخفية.. وذلك لا رخصة فى ذكره.. وقد يجوز إظهاره حتى لا يقع
المغرور فيها.. وبالله التوفيق.. وهو حسبى ونعم الوكيل.. ولا حول ولا قوة
إلا بالله  العظيم..
تم ذلك بحمد الله وعونه على يد كاتبه لنفسه ولمن شاء الله من بعده راجى
عفو ربه القريب المجيب الفقير عثمان ابن العلامة الشيخ سلمان الشافعى
السويفى غفر الله ولوالديه وللمسلمين.. وصلى الله على محمد وآله وصحبه.

- Root: خ-د-ع (kh-d-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deception, trickery, concealment of intent; the inner state contradicting the outward show.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul’s self-deception (ghurūr) as a spiritual ailment — the deluded one mistakes the means for the end.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: actual fraud; metaphorical: the soul’s veiling of truth from itself.
- Root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A screen, curtain, partition; that which conceals.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The seventy veils (ḥujub) between the servant and God — light and darkness — as stages of proximity and distance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical barrier; metaphorical: every perception or state that blocks vision of the Real.
- Root: م-ش-ك-ا-ة (m-sh-k-āh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A niche, recess in a wall for a lamp.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Light Verse {«…كَمِشْكَاةٍ…»} — the niche as the receptacle of the lamp, symbolizing the heart’s container for divine light.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: architectural niche; metaphorical: the bodily or psychic veil that screens the heart’s light.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — e.g., “فإن لم يتضح ما وراء ذلك ووقف عنك هلك” — the protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (result), marking the causal necessity of perdition upon stopping.
chapters.translation:
I say: The sixth category — another group claimed good character, humility, and generosity, and they devoted themselves to serving the Sufis. So they gathered people and undertook their service, making of that a net for the chaff of this world and a means of amassing wealth. Their true aim was only to multiply their numbers and magnify their repute, while they displayed that their aim was service and subordination. Then they would collect from the unlawful and the dubious (shubuhāt) to spend upon them, so that their followers would increase and their names be spread abroad through service. Some of them take from the wealth of the sultan and spend it upon them; others take it to spend on the Sufis along the pilgrimage route, claiming that their aim is piety and expenditure. But the motive of all of them is ostentation (riyāʾ) and seeking repute (sumʿah). This is so by their neglect of all the commands of God Most High, outwardly, and their contentment with taking the unlawful and spending from it. The likeness of this is like one who spends his wealth on the pilgrims’ road, or like one who builds a mosque of God Most High and plasters it with filth, yet claims his intent is construction.

The seventh category — another group occupied themselves with spiritual striving (mujāhadah), the refinement of character, and the purification of the soul from its defects. They plunged deep into this, and took the investigation of the soul’s faults and the knowledge of its deception as a science and a craft for themselves. So in all states they busy themselves with examining the soul’s defects and extracting subtle discourse concerning its afflictions. They say: “This is a defect in the soul,” and “negligence in deeming it a defect is itself a defect.” They occupy themselves with entangled words, wasting their times therein, as if they had halted with their own selves and not busied themselves with their Creator. Their likeness is the likeness of one who busies himself with the times of the pilgrimage and its obstacles, yet does not traverse the pilgrimage road — and that avails him nothing of the pilgrimage.

The eighth category — another group surpassed this rank and began to traverse the path, and the doors of knowledge (maʿrifah) opened to them. Whenever they smelled a fragrance from the beginnings of knowledge, they marveled at it and rejoiced in it, and its planting pleased them. So their hearts became attached to turning toward it and reflecting upon it, and upon how its door opened to them while it remained closed to others. All of that is delusion (ghurūr), for the wonders of God’s path have no end. Whoever halts at every wonder and is bound by it — his steps fall short, and he is deprived of reaching the goal. His likeness is the likeness of one who came before a king, and saw at the gate of his arena a garden with flowers and lights, which he had never seen before nor seen its like. He stood gazing at it until the time in which he could meet the king passed him by, and he departed disappointed.

The ninth category — another group surpassed these, and did not turn toward what overflowed upon them of lights upon the path, nor toward the abundant gifts made easy for them. They did not look at them, nor did they alight upon them, but were earnest in journeying. When they drew near to arrival, they thought that they had arrived, so they halted and did not go beyond that — and they erred. For God has seventy veils of light and darkness, and no wayfarer reaches a veil of those veils but he thinks that he has arrived. To this points His saying, Most High, telling of Abraham, upon him the most excellent prayer and peace, when he said: {«فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأَىٰ كَوْكَبًا»} — the verse. And how numerous are the veils in this station!

The first veil between the servant and his Lord is his very self (nafs). For it is a mighty lordly matter, and it is a light from the lights of God Most High — I mean the secret of the heart (sirr al-qalb), which will disclose the reality of the Truth as it is, so that it hears the whole of the world entirely and the forms of all creatures encompass it. At that time its light will shine with a mighty radiance, for all existence will appear in it as it is. And in its first state it is veiled by a niche (mishkāh) that screens it. When its light shines forth and the beauty of the heart is unveiled after the radiance of God’s light falls upon it, perhaps the possessor of the heart turns to the heart and sees of its surpassing beauty what astonishes him. Then perhaps he declares plainly and says: “I am the Truth (anā al-ḥaqq).” For if what lies beyond that is not clarified, and he halts, he perishes. With this very eye the Christians looked upon the Messiah, upon him peace, when they saw the radiance of God’s light upon him — and they erred, like one who sees a star in a mirror or in water, and thinks that the star is the mirror, so he stretches his hand to take it — he is deluded.

Are there yet other kinds upon the path of wayfaring? The kinds of delusion upon the path of wayfaring to God cannot be exhausted except by explaining all the hidden sciences, and there is no license to mention that. Yet it may be permissible to disclose it, so that the deluded one does not fall into it. And with God is success; He suffices me, and He is the best disposer of affairs. There is no might and no power except with God, the Mighty.

It is completed, by the praise of God and His aid, at the hand of its writer for himself and for whomsoever God wills after him, hoping for the pardon of his Lord, the Near, the Responsive — the poor ʿUthmān, son of the distinguished scholar Shaykh Salmān al-Shāfiʿī al-Suwayfī. May God forgive him, his parents, and the Muslims. And may God bless Muḥammad, his family, and his companions. PageV01P075.
